title: A modifier value agrees with one selected argument class
summary: A narrow agreement model makes a modifier form depend on the class of one designated argument, while other neighboring arguments may vary freely.

design.unit: multi-argument records with one modifier and independently typed argument candidates
design.contrast: agreement with designated argument versus free modifier attachment
design.prediction: Holding the modifier constant, changing only the designated argument class should force the licensed modifier alternation; changing a non-designated argument should not.
design.countermodel: The same surface pattern could arise from a context-conditioned lexical convention or editorial packaging without the proposed semantic mechanism.
design.falsifier: A matched change to the designated class leaves the modifier unchanged while a non-designated change triggers it, under fixed record scope.
design.principal_risk: Argument classes and modifier meanings lack independent bindings. Near argument-role cards, but the falsifier tests a selection rule rather than role frequency or position.
